short: Labour's return to power after fourteen years, on a very low share of the vote.
full:
Keir Starmer, previously Director of Public Prosecutions, became prime minister on 5 July 2024 after Labour won 411 seats. The majority of 174 was among the largest the party has ever held, but it rested on just under thirty-four per cent of the vote, the lowest share ever recorded for a majority government, on the lowest turnout since 2001.

His government inherited weak growth and stretched public finances, and its first budget raised taxes by around forty billion pounds, most of it through employers' national insurance. It legislated to create Great British Energy, began taking rail franchises into public ownership as contracts expired, and passed an employment rights bill restricting zero-hours contracts and qualifying periods for unfair dismissal. Abroad he signed a reset agreement with the European Union in May 2025 and helped coordinate European support for Ukraine. Reform UK led the opinion polls within a year of the election.
